venue.name: Ocean Networks Canada - Marine Technology Centre
venue.description: Ocean Networks Canada is a University of Victoria initiative that operates cabled ocean observatories on Canada's Pacific, Atlantic and Arctic coasts and in the Southern Ocean. Its Marine Technology Centre is on West Saanich Road in North Saanich. Its programs for children are school presentations delivered in the classroom or online, plus annual events held in other communities. The site does not describe any tour, open house or visit at this address.
venue.address: #106, 9865 West Saanich Road, North Saanich, BC, Canada, V8L 5Y8

programs.name: ONC school presentation
programs.description: Ocean Networks Canada runs interactive presentations for schools, either in person at your school or online. They are aligned with the British Columbia public school curriculum and are designed and delivered by ONC's own team of BC certified teachers, covering ocean science, Indigenous knowledge and ONC's ocean data. Booking goes through their online registration system.
programs.what_children_do: Sit together in their own classroom while an ONC teacher works through ocean science, Indigenous knowledge and live ocean data, with interactive parts and questions along the way.
programs.our_note: This one comes to you, so there is no bus and no travel time to plan. Their page points at middle and high school students, so if your children are younger, ask what they can actually offer before you build a day around it.
programs.practical_summary: The session happens in your own room, so washrooms, lunch and parking are your own. What the site does not say is the cost, how long a session runs or which grades they will take, so ask all three when you register.
programs.evidence: ONC’s interactive presentations are aligned with the British Columbia public school curriculum and are designed and delivered by our team of BC certified teachers.

programs.name: Ship2Shore live link
programs.description: A live video link with Ocean Networks Canada during an at sea expedition. Classes join by video conference and can ask scientists, engineers and ship crew about ocean science, technology and life at sea. Expedition dates move each year, but these sessions usually fall between May and September. Their page lists what you need at your end: an internet connection, Zoom, a projector or screen, speakers and a keyboard.
programs.what_children_do: Watch and talk to scientists and crew on a working ship over a video call, and put their own questions to them.
programs.our_note: It all happens on your screen in your own room, so the day stands or falls on your internet and a working projector. Sailing dates change every year, so ask early which weeks are on offer.
programs.practical_summary: There is no travel and no building to ask about, just your own room and a screen. The cost, the length of a session and how far ahead to book are all unpublished.
programs.evidence: Using video conferencing, participants onshore can connect live with scientists, engineers, and ship crew to discuss ocean science, technology, and life at sea.

programs.name: Ocean Science Symposium
programs.description: An annual Ocean Networks Canada event for middle and high school students, held in a different community around British Columbia each year. It is invitation only and there is no cost. Activities and interactive sessions cover careers, current research, Indigenous knowledge, science and technology in the ocean sector.
programs.what_children_do: Take part in activities and interactive sessions with ocean scientists, and hear about current research and the jobs behind it.
programs.our_note: You cannot simply book this one, it is invitation only. If it sounds right for your group, email the learning team and ask how schools get on the list.
programs.practical_summary: It costs nothing, but it is invitation only and the location moves each year, so where you would go, how long it runs and which ages it suits are all unpublished.
programs.evidence: ONC’s annual Ocean Science Symposium is a no cost invitation-only event held in various communities across BC

A darkened control room with a wall of screens showing underwater camera views, and a red digital counter above them.

gaps: No price is published for the school presentations or for Ship2Shore. Any fee is only visible once you are inside their registration system.

No grade or age range is published for the school presentations. The page names middle and high school students, the section around it is called Youth Programs K-12, and the testimonials include elementary teachers.
Session length, maximum class size and minimum booking notice are not stated anywhere.
No youngest age is given. The youth programs are written for middle and high school, so a daycare group would have to ask whether anything at all is offered for under fives.

The Annual Events page keeps its detail inside collapsed panels that a plain fetch does not return. The Ocean Science Symposium and Ship2Shore details here were read with those panels opened in a browser.
No latitude and longitude are published anywhere on the site, so the street address is recorded and geocoding is still to be done.
The Open Graph image on the contact page is the web agency's wordmark rather than a photograph, so it was not used.
The site never describes a visit, tour or open house at the Marine Technology Centre in North Saanich. Everything found is delivered at your school, over video, or at events held in other places.

The programs listed here belong to Ocean Networks Canada as an organisation, not to this building. The same three appear on the record for their Ocean-Climate Building in Victoria, and booking for both goes to the same learning team.
Because the site offers no visits to this address, nothing is published about washrooms, lunch space, bus parking or step free access here.
No photograph of the Marine Technology Centre building appears on the site, so the images here are general Ocean Networks Canada photos.
